title: Synonym, Antonym, Idiom, and Proverbs — Level 10 — Final challenge

items.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses the idiom "break a leg" correctly.

visual.text: Before Ayu went on stage, her friends told her to break a leg.

choices.say: Before Ayu went on stage, her friends told her to break a leg.

visual.text: The test was so easy; it was a real break a leg.

choices.say: The test was so easy; it was a real break a leg.

visual.text: Raka was so sleepy that he wanted to break a leg.

choices.say: Raka was so sleepy that he wanted to break a leg.

visual.text: Dimas broke a leg, so he finished the race first.

choices.say: Dimas broke a leg, so he finished the race first.

items.reteach: "Break a leg" = semoga sukses, diucapkan sebelum seseorang tampil.

items.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses the idiom "under the weather" correctly.

visual.text: Dimas stayed home from school because he was under the weather.

choices.say: Dimas stayed home from school because he was under the weather.

visual.text: We had a picnic under the weather in the park.

choices.say: We had a picnic under the weather in the park.

visual.text: Ayu was under the weather after winning first prize, so she danced happily.

choices.say: Ayu was under the weather after winning first prize, so she danced happily.

visual.text: The sky is under the weather, so the sun is shining.

choices.say: The sky is under the weather, so the sun is shining.

items.reteach: "Under the weather" = kurang sehat, sehingga cocok dengan alasan tidak masuk sekolah.

items.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses the idiom "once in a blue moon" correctly.

visual.text: My uncle lives abroad, so he visits us once in a blue moon.

choices.say: My uncle lives abroad, so he visits us once in a blue moon.

visual.text: I brush my teeth once in a blue moon every morning.

choices.say: I brush my teeth once in a blue moon every morning.

visual.text: We eat breakfast once in a blue moon because we have it every day.

choices.say: We eat breakfast once in a blue moon because we have it every day.

visual.text: Sinta goes to school once in a blue moon from Monday to Friday.

choices.say: Sinta goes to school once in a blue moon from Monday to Friday.

items.reteach: "Once in a blue moon" = sangat jarang. Tidak cocok dengan kegiatan harian.

items.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses the idiom "cost an arm and a leg" correctly.

visual.text: The new laptop cost an arm and a leg, so Dad saved for months.

choices.say: The new laptop cost an arm and a leg, so Dad saved for months.

visual.text: The pencil was very cheap; it cost an arm and a leg.

choices.say: The pencil was very cheap; it cost an arm and a leg.

visual.text: Sinta cost an arm and a leg when she fell off her bike.

choices.say: Sinta cost an arm and a leg when she fell off her bike.

visual.text: The free concert cost an arm and a leg for everyone.

choices.say: The free concert cost an arm and a leg for everyone.

items.reteach: "Cost an arm and a leg" = sangat mahal.

items.prompt: Choose the sentence that is correct about antonyms.
items.reteach: Shallow (dangkal) berlawanan dengan deep (dalam). Wide–broad dan ancient–old bersinonim.

items.prompt: Choose the sentence that is correct about synonyms.
items.reteach: Begin = commence (mulai). Pasangan lainnya berlawanan arti.

items.prompt: Find the word that is kurang tepat in this proverb: "The early bird catches the fish."
items.reteach: Peribahasa aslinya: "The early bird catches the worm."

items.prompt: Find the word that is kurang tepat in this proverb: "Don't judge a book by its page."
items.reteach: Peribahasa aslinya: "Don't judge a book by its cover."

items.prompt: Find the word that is kurang tepat in this proverb: "Many hands make heavy work."
items.reteach: Peribahasa aslinya: "Many hands make light work" (banyak tangan membuat pekerjaan ringan).

items.prompt: Find the word that is kurang tepat in this proverb: "Actions speak quieter than words."
items.reteach: Peribahasa aslinya: "Actions speak louder than words."

items.prompt: Find the word that is kurang tepat in this idiom: "It's getting late. Let's call it the day and go home."
items.reteach: Idiom yang benar: "call it a day" (mengakhiri pekerjaan hari ini).

items.prompt: Find the word that is kurang tepat in this idiom: "Sinta spilled the peas and told everyone about the surprise party."
items.reteach: Idiom yang benar: "spill the beans" (membocorkan rahasia).

items.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses the idiom "hit the sack" correctly.

visual.text: It's almost midnight, so I'm going to hit the sack.

choices.say: It's almost midnight, so I'm going to hit the sack.

visual.text: Raka hit the sack, so he stayed wide awake all night.

choices.say: Raka hit the sack, so he stayed wide awake all night.

visual.text: We hit the sack at noon to start our school day.

choices.say: We hit the sack at noon to start our school day.

visual.text: Ayu hit the sack because she wanted to stay up late.

choices.say: Ayu hit the sack because she wanted to stay up late.

items.reteach: "Hit the sack" = pergi tidur.

items.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses the proverb "Better late than never" correctly.

visual.text: Rudi handed in his homework a day late, but better late than never.

choices.say: Rudi handed in his homework a day late, but better late than never.

visual.text: The bus came ten minutes early; better late than never.

choices.say: The bus came ten minutes early; better late than never.

visual.text: Better late than never, so always come to class late.

choices.say: Better late than never, so always come to class late.

visual.text: I arrived exactly on time, so it was better late than never.

choices.say: I arrived exactly on time, so it was better late than never.

items.reteach: "Better late than never" dipakai saat sesuatu terlambat tetapi tetap dilakukan.

items.prompt: Read the story about Raka's debate. What did the coach mean by "Break a leg!"?

stimulus.text: Raka was nervous about the debate. His coach said, "Break a leg!" Raka smiled, took a deep breath, and spoke clearly. In the end, the judges praised his confident voice.

items.reteach: Idiom "Break a leg" = semoga sukses sebelum tampil.

items.prompt: In the story about Raka's debate, which word is closest in meaning to "praised"?

stimulus.text: Raka was nervous about the debate. His coach said, "Break a leg!" Raka smiled, took a deep breath, and spoke clearly. In the end, the judges praised his confident voice.

items.reteach: Praise = memuji = compliment. Criticise justru mengkritik.

items.prompt: In the story about Raka's debate, which word is the antonym of "nervous" as it is used at the start?

stimulus.text: Raka was nervous about the debate. His coach said, "Break a leg!" Raka smiled, took a deep breath, and spoke clearly. In the end, the judges praised his confident voice.

items.reteach: Nervous = gugup. Antonimnya calm (tenang). Anxious, worried, tense bermakna mirip nervous.

items.prompt: Read the story about Sinta's savings. What is the main lesson of the story?

stimulus.text: Sinta saved a little of her pocket money every week. After a year, she had enough to buy a bicycle. Her mother smiled and said, "See? Slow and steady wins the race."

visual.text: Small, regular efforts can lead to success.

choices.say: Small, regular efforts can lead to success.

visual.text: Bicycles are too expensive for children.

choices.say: Bicycles are too expensive for children.

visual.text: Mothers should buy bicycles for their children.

choices.say: Mothers should buy bicycles for their children.

visual.text: Pocket money should be spent every week.

choices.say: Pocket money should be spent every week.

items.reteach: Main lesson: menabung sedikit demi sedikit secara teratur akhirnya berhasil.

items.prompt: Which proverb has a similar message to the story about Sinta's savings?

stimulus.text: Sinta saved a little of her pocket money every week. After a year, she had enough to buy a bicycle. Her mother smiled and said, "See? Slow and steady wins the race."

visual.text: Rome wasn't built in a day.

choices.say: Rome wasn't built in a day.

visual.text: Don't judge a book by its cover.

choices.say: Don't judge a book by its cover.

visual.text: Too many cooks spoil the broth.

choices.say: Too many cooks spoil the broth.

visual.text: Out of sight, out of mind.

choices.say: Out of sight, out of mind.

items.reteach: "Rome wasn't built in a day" = hal besar butuh waktu dan usaha bertahap.

items.prompt: In the story about Sinta's savings, "steady" in "Slow and steady wins the race" means …

stimulus.text: Sinta saved a little of her pocket money every week. After a year, she had enough to buy a bicycle. Her mother smiled and said, "See? Slow and steady wins the race."

items.reteach: Steady = ajek, teratur, terus-menerus.

items.prompt: Read the notice from the school canteen. What is its purpose?

stimulus.text: Dear students, from Monday the school canteen will stop using plastic straws. This step may seem minor, but every little helps to keep our rivers and oceans clean.

visual.text: to tell students about a change that helps the environment

choices.say: to tell students about a change that helps the environment

visual.text: to advertise a new drink at the canteen

choices.say: to advertise a new drink at the canteen

visual.text: to ask students to bring plastic straws

choices.say: to ask students to bring plastic straws

visual.text: to announce that the canteen will close

choices.say: to announce that the canteen will close

items.reteach: Purpose: memberi tahu perubahan (berhenti memakai sedotan plastik) demi lingkungan.

items.prompt: In the canteen notice, the word "minor" is closest in meaning to …

stimulus.text: Dear students, from Monday the school canteen will stop using plastic straws. This step may seem minor, but every little helps to keep our rivers and oceans clean.

items.reteach: Minor = kecil/tidak penting. Antonimnya major.

items.prompt: In the canteen notice, "every little helps" means …

stimulus.text: Dear students, from Monday the school canteen will stop using plastic straws. This step may seem minor, but every little helps to keep our rivers and oceans clean.

visual.text: small actions together can make a difference

choices.say: small actions together can make a difference

visual.text: little children should help at the canteen

choices.say: little children should help at the canteen

items.reteach: "Every little helps" = sekecil apa pun, setiap usaha ada manfaatnya.

items.prompt: Analogy: Hot is to cold as ancient is to …

items.prompt: Analogy: Big is to huge as small is to …

items.prompt: Odd one out: glad, cheerful, delighted, gloomy. Which word does not belong?

items.prompt: Which pair is NOT a pair of antonyms?

items.prompt: Riddle: "I am not a vegetable you cook, but people spill me when they tell a secret." What am I?

items.prompt: Which colour completes all three idioms: "once in a ___ moon", "feeling ___", and "out of the ___"?
items.reteach: Once in a blue moon (sangat jarang), feeling blue (sedih), out of the blue (tiba-tiba).

items.prompt: Which animal completes both: "It's raining ___s and dogs" and "let the ___ out of the bag"?
items.reteach: Raining cats and dogs (hujan deras) dan let the cat out of the bag (membocorkan rahasia).

items.prompt: Unscramble T-N-E-I-C-A-N to get the antonym of "modern".
items.reteach: TNEICAN = ANCIENT (kuno), lawan dari modern.

items.prompt: Which body part completes both idioms: "cost an ___ and a leg" and "twist someone's ___"?
items.reteach: Cost an arm and a leg (sangat mahal); twist someone's arm (membujuk dengan memaksa).

items.prompt: Code: S = synonym pair, A = antonym pair. What is the code for these pairs in order: begin – start, rich – poor, smart – clever?
items.reteach: Begin–start sinonim (S), rich–poor antonim (A), smart–clever sinonim (S).

items.prompt: Riddle: "I am a proverb. I say that you should use your hours well because they are as valuable as money." Which proverb am I?
items.reteach: "Time is money" = waktu itu berharga. "Time flies" = waktu berlalu cepat.

items.prompt: How many of these words are synonyms of "happy": glad, joyful, content, miserable, cheerful?
items.reteach: Glad, joyful, content, cheerful = senang (4). Miserable = sangat sedih.

items.prompt: Analogy: "Over the moon" is to happy as "feeling blue" is to …
items.reteach: Over the moon = sangat senang; feeling blue = sedih.
